tools.name: animation_editor
tools.description: Creates and modifies animations (state machines, linear animations, keyframes) on the active artboard. Falls back to the first artboard when none is activated; use query_core_object_tool.listArtboards to disambiguate. Special state names: "{Entry State}", "{Any State}". Between two keyframes the smaller-frame keyframe's interpolator (hold/linear/cubic/elastic) drives the curve. Commands: createStateMachine, createStateMachineLayers, createTransitions, createConditions, createLinearAnimations: create the named entity; createStates: Add new animation states to an EXISTING layer (use this when the layer already exists; createStateMachineLayers spawns a new layer instead); listStateMachines: id/name/layers only — for inspection use queryStateMachine; listLinearAnimations: all linear animations; queryStateMachine: PRIMARY read. Fully expands a state machine — layers with states/transitions/conditions/events/listenerActions, plus top-level inputs and listeners. View-model, event, and input refs are pre-resolved with names. Defaults to the only state machine; pass stateMachineId to disambiguate; queryStateMachineLayer: Re-read one layer (same per-layer payload); updateStates: Update existing states; renameAnimations: Rename animations; modifyKeyFrames: Add/delete/change keyframes; queryKeyFrames: Read keyframes; reverseKeyFrames: Reverse keyframes (scope: selection, else visible graph curves, else all). Data is passed under data.<command> or directly in data.

stateMachineId.description: Optional. Defaults to the only state machine in the active artboard.

layerId.description: ID of an existing state machine layer.

linearAnimationName.description: Name of an existing linear animation on the artboard. If unresolvable, the state is still created but a warning is emitted.

transitions.description: Inline transitions; from/to match state names declared in this same payload.

oneOf.description: for values that are colors, format is #aarrggbb

interpolationType.description: The interpolation type for the keyframe to determine the value in between two keyframes:hold: hold the incoming value until the next keyframe is reached;linear: linearly interpolate;cubic: cubicly interpolate with parameters;

cubicParams.description: Parameters for cubic interpolation. x1, x2 in [0, 1], y1, y2 in [-1, 1]

amplitude.description: A percentage of change, defaults to 1.0

period.description: Percentage of time difference, defaults to 1.0

oneOf.description: for values that are colors, format is #aarrggbb

interpolationType.description: The interpolation type for the keyframe to determine the value in between two keyframes:hold: hold the incoming value until the next keyframe is reached;linear: linearly interpolate;cubic: cubicly interpolate with parameters;

cubicParams.description: Parameters for cubic interpolation. x1, x2 in [0, 1], y1, y2 in [-1, 1]

amplitude.description: A percentage of change, defaults to 1.0

period.description: Percentage of time difference, defaults to 1.0

delete.description: List of keyframe IDs to delete

animationIds.description: List of linear animation IDs to query. Defaults to the selected linear animation if not provided.

tools.name: assets_tool
tools.description: Read and instantiate assets (images, audio, fonts, scripts, libraries, components, blobs, svg, lottie). listAssets: Folder-grouped tree; queryAsset: One asset by id; addImageInstance: Spawn an Image shape from an ImageAsset; addImagesAsSolo: Spawn a Solo of Images (no input/VM wiring).

typeFilter.description: Optional. One of: image, audio, font, script, library, component, svg, lottie, file, folder, group, componentGroup. Folders are still walked.

tools.name: component_editor
tools.description: Adds Components to other Artboards. When a Component Artboard has a ViewModel bound, we should try to hook it up to the parent Artboard's ViewModel as a property. Supports commands like,addComponents: Adds a Component as a child of the given parent on the specified artboard; addComponentList: Adds a Component list container as a child of the given parent on the specified artboard where the parent determines the list's layout. A Component List automatically generates component instances at runtime based on the specified ViewModelPropertyList id so DO NOT manually add Components as children of the list. Use instead of 'addComponents' whenever a list of items is required;

artboardName.description: The name of the artboard target

parentId.description: The ID of the object that should be the Components immediate parent

componentId.description: The ID of the component to add to the artboard

mode.description: The mode of the component to add which determines how it behaves when it resizes. node = stretches, leaf = scales with proportions, alignment, layout = does not scale, but resizes and reflows its internal layout contents

widthScaleType.description: The width scale type of the component when in layout mode. fixed = fixed size, fill = fills its parent layout, hug = lets its children determine its size

heightScaleType.description: The height scale type of the component when in layout mode. fixed = fixed size, fill = fills its parent layout, hug = lets its children determine its size

x.description: The X position of the component in the artboard

y.description: The Y position of the component in the artboard

artboardName.description: The name of the artboard target

parentId.description: The ID of the object that should be the Components immediate parent

viewModelPropertyListId.description: The ID of the ViewModelPropertyList to populate the Component list

tools.name: layout_editor
tools.description:
Creates UI layouts with flexbox-style positioning, padding, gaps, and alignment. Use this for structured user interfaces.

USE THIS TOOL for:
- UI components (buttons, cards, modals, navigation bars)
- Screen layouts and page structures
- Lists, grids, and content containers
- Text with layout positioning (do NOT use emoji characters)
- Anything requiring flexbox arrangement (rows, columns, wrapping)

Commands: createLayout (new layout tree), appendLayout (add children)

tools.name: property_group_editor
tools.description: Creates Custom Property Groups and the typed Custom Properties they contain on a parent (artboard or any container component). The resulting properties can be data-bound (use viewmodel_editor databind with the property's id and returned bindKey) and keyframed on a timeline (use animation_editor with the same id and returned keyframeKey, which is type-specific such as firePropertyKey for triggers). Property types: number, boolean, color, string, enum, trigger. Commands: addPropertyGroups: Creates one or more property groups, each with an optional initial set of properties; addPropertiesToGroup: Adds properties to an existing group.

parentId.description: ID of the parent ContainerComponent (artboard or any container component) to attach the group to.

name.description: Optional name for the property group.

properties.description: List of typed custom properties to create in the group.

value.description: Optional initial value. number=double, boolean=bool, color=#aarrggbb string, string=string, enum=enum value name (matched against the enum referenced by enumId), trigger ignored.

enumId.description: Required for enum properties: id of the DataEnum that defines this property's allowed values.

groupId.description: ID of the existing CustomPropertyGroup to add properties to.

properties.description: List of typed custom properties to create in the group.

value.description: Optional initial value. number=double, boolean=bool, color=#aarrggbb string, string=string, enum=enum value name (matched against the enum referenced by enumId), trigger ignored.

enumId.description: Required for enum properties: id of the DataEnum that defines this property's allowed values.

tools.name: viewmodel_editor
tools.description: Creates and manages view models and their instances. Supports commands like,listViewModels: Lists all view models; createViewModels: Creates view models with properties; createViewModelInstances: Creates instances of a view model; addProperties: Adds properties to existing view models; databind: Makes the value of an object's property come from a viewmodel instance. When binding strings to text, you must bind to the Text Run, not the Text object itself; modifyDataBind: Modifies an existing data bind's direction (toTarget, toSource, twoWay), once flag, source-to-target ordering, or attached converter; bindViewModelToArtboard: Binds a viewmodel instance to an artboard; bindViewModelToComponent: Binds a viewmodel instance to a component; listViewModelInstances: Lists all view model instances from a view model;

viewModelId.description: The ID of the view model to bind to

objectId.description: The ID of the object to bind

propertyKey.description: The property key of the object property to bind

viewModelPropertyId.description: The ID of the view model property to bind to

objectId.description: ID of the object whose existing bind to modify

propertyKey.description: Property key on the object whose bind to modify

direction.description: Optional. Sets the primary direction bit independently of twoWay. toTarget = ViewModel -> Object (the default for a new bind); toSource = Object -> ViewModel. When twoWay is also true, this still determines which side the converter treats as input vs output.

twoWay.description: Optional. Enable bidirectional sync. Independent of direction — leave direction unset to preserve the existing primary direction.

once.description: Optional. If true, the bind is applied only once.

sourceToTargetRunsFirst.description: Optional. For two-way binds, when true source-to-target runs before target-to-source.

converterId.description: Optional. ID of a DataConverter to attach. Pass empty string to remove an existing converter.

artboardId.description: The ID of the artboard to bind the viewmodel to

viewModelId.description: The ID of the viewmodel to bind

viewModelInstanceId.description: Optional: The ID of a specific viewmodel instance. If not provided, uses the first instance.

componentId.description: The ID of the Component to bind the viewmodel to

viewModelPropertyName.description: The name of the viewmodel property (of type viewmodel) on the parent Artboards viewmodel to bind to the component. If the property doesnt exist, create it. We should not allow duplicate viewmodel property names.

viewModelInstanceName.description: Optional: The name of a specific viewmodel instance, each Component typically needs a unique instance. If not provided or it is not found, we create a new instance for the Component.

viewModelId.description: The ID of the viewmodel to list its instances

tools.name: path_editor
tools.description:
Creates shapes in Rive composed by paths. IMPORTANT: A shape is invisible without paths AND commands. Every shape MUST have at least one path with at least one moveTo and one lineTo/cubicTo. Every filled path MUST end with a close command. VALID paintType values (exact strings): "fill" or "stroke". VALID commandType values (exact strings): "moveTo" (requires x,y — sets the start point), "lineTo" (requires x,y — draws a straight segment), "cubicTo" (requires control1X,control1Y,control2X,control2Y,endX,endY — bezier curve), "close" (no args — closes the path back to moveTo point, required for fills). EXAMPLE — red 50×50 square at (200,200): {"name":"Box","x":200,"y":200,"paints":[{"paintType":"fill","color":"#FFFF0000"}],"paths":[{"name":"P","commands":[{"commandType":"moveTo","x":-25,"y":-25},{"commandType":"lineTo","x":25,"y":-25},{"commandType":"lineTo","x":25,"y":25},{"commandType":"lineTo","x":-25,"y":25},{"commandType":"close"}]}]}. COORDINATE SYSTEM: A shape's x/y are in its PARENT's local space. Path commands are in the shape's OWN local space, drawn around (0,0). A layout's origin is its TOP-LEFT corner. A shape's x/y positions its center relative to that. To align a shape inside a layout, wrap it in a child layout the same size as the shape, set the PARENT layout's alignment, and place the shape at x=W/2, y=H/2 inside the child layout. Supports commands: createShapes: Creates shapes with paths and paints; addVertices: Adds vertices to an existing PointsPath by ID; addPaths: Adds new paths to an existing Shape by ID; addPaints: Adds new fills or strokes to an existing Shape by ID; 

USE THIS TOOL for:
- Rectangles, squares, triangles, polygons
- Circles, ellipses, arcs
- Simple lines, arrows, or connectors
- Basic geometric patterns
- Shapes you can describe with coordinates

parentId.description: The ID of the object that should be the shape's parent

x.description: The X position of the shape's origin in its PARENT's local space (not world space). Path commands are relative to this origin. When inside a layout, prefer using a child layout with alignment rather than computing offsets manually.

y.description: The Y position of the shape's origin in its PARENT's local space (not world space). Path commands are relative to this origin. When inside a layout, prefer using a child layout with alignment rather than computing offsets manually.

paints.description: Fills and strokes for this shape. paintType must be the exact string "fill" or "stroke". Filled shapes require all paths to end with close.

feather.description: Optional soft edge / blur effect on this paint.

offsetX.description: X offset of the feather. Default 0.

offsetY.description: Y offset of the feather. Default 0.

inner.description: True for an inner feather (soft inner edge / inner glow). Default false (outer).

width.description: the width of the stroke of this paint

feather.description: Optional soft edge / blur effect on this paint.

offsetX.description: X offset of the feather. Default 0.

offsetY.description: Y offset of the feather. Default 0.

inner.description: True for an inner feather (soft inner edge / inner glow). Default false (outer).

paths.description: a list of paths that are grouped by the shape and have the shape's paints applied to them. Each path command should have at most one close command

commands.description: Drawing commands. commandType must be the exact string "moveTo" (x,y), "lineTo" (x,y), "cubicTo" (control1X,control1Y,control2X,control2Y,endX,endY), or "close" (no args). A path with no commands is invisible.

oneOf.description: Moves the pen to a new starting point without drawing anything.

x.description: the x position of this move to command

y.description: the y position of this move to command

oneOf.description: Draws a straight line from the current pen position to (x, y).

x.description: the x position of this line to command

y.description: the y position of this line to command

oneOf.description: Draws a cubic bezier curve from the current point to (endX, endY) using two control points (control1X, control1Y) and (control2X, control2Y).

control1X.description: the control1 X position of this bezier command

control1Y.description: the control1 Y position of this bezier command

control2X.description: the control2 X position of this bezier command

control2Y.description: the control2 Y position of this bezier command

endX.description: the end X position of this bezier command

endY.description: the end Y position of this bezier command

oneOf.description: Closes the current path by drawing a straight line from the current point back to the starting point of the path.

pathId.description: The ID of the PointsPath to add vertices to. Use getArtboardHierarchy to find it.

x.description: X position in the path's local space.

y.description: Y position in the path's local space.

type.description: straight = sharp corner (no handles). cubic = smooth curve with independent in/out handles.

inX.description: X of the in control-point handle (cubic only).

inY.description: Y of the in control-point handle (cubic only).

outX.description: X of the out control-point handle (cubic only).

outY.description: Y of the out control-point handle (cubic only).

insertAfterVertexId.description: Optional. ID of an existing vertex to insert after. If omitted the vertex is appended at the end.

addPaths.description: Adds one or more new PointsPaths to an existing Shape.

shapeId.description: ID of the Shape to add paths to. Use getArtboardHierarchy to find it.

addPaints.description: Adds one or more new fills or strokes to an existing Shape.

shapeId.description: ID of the Shape to add paints to. Use getArtboardHierarchy to find it.

paints.description: Paint definitions to add (same format as createShapes).

tools.name: query_property_keys
tools.description: Get the available properties on objects by object IDs. Returns human-readable property names mapped to integer keys. Enum-backed properties also include an `enums` entry (propertyKey -> [name0, name1, ...]); the array index is the uint value to pass to set_property_values.

objectIds.description: Array of object IDs to query properties for

animates.description: Include only properties that can be animated

binds.description: Include only properties that can be used in databind

tools.name: query_objects
tools.description: Get id, type, name, and children for objects (depth-limited). If objectIds are not provided, defaults to currently selected objects.

objectIds.description: Array of object IDs to query for. If not provided, defaults to currently selected objects.

depth.description: Maximum depth to traverse children (0 = no children, 1 = direct children only, etc.). Defaults to 5 if not provided.

tools.name: query_property_values
tools.description: Get current values for object properties by object IDs and property keys.

propertyKeys.description: Object Id to array of property keys to get values for.

tools.name: find_objects
tools.description: Search for objects in the active artboard by name (case-insensitive substring) and/or type string. Use this to find an object ID when you only know its name or type.

name.description: Case-insensitive substring to match against object names. Omit to match any name.

type.description: Type string to filter by (e.g. "shape", "rectangle", "text", "group", "node", "ellipse", "artboard"). Omit to match any type.

parentId.description: Restrict the search to children of this object ID. Omit to search the entire active artboard.

tools.name: get_artboard_hierarchy
tools.description: Get the object tree of an artboard. Use depth=2 or depth=3 for a broad overview, then drill into specific branches. Avoid depth > 6 on complex artboards — the response can be very large.

artboardId.description: ID of the artboard to get the hierarchy for. Defaults to the active artboard if not provided.

depth.description: Maximum depth to traverse. Defaults to 5. Start shallow and increase only if you need to see deeper nesting. Large artboards at depth 20 can produce thousands of tokens.

tools.name: list_artboards
tools.description: List all artboards (id, name, isActive). For "what is the user working on": prefer selectionArtboardId (current selection) over isActive (sticky — persists across deselects).

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: Returns the id, name, types, and parent id of every currently selected object in the editor.

inputSchema.description: Takes no input. Returns the currently selected objects in the editor.

tools.name: set_property_values
tools.description: Set values for object properties by object IDs and property keys. Invalid writes are rejected per-property in an errors list with machine-readable codes (invalid_enum_value, unknown_id, type_mismatch, read_only, ...).

propertyValues.description: Object Id to map of property keys to values: Map<Id, Map<int, int|string|color|bool>>

additionalProperties.description: Map of property keys to values. Values should match the property type (string, boolean, number, color string like #aarrggbb, or Id string).

tools.name: delete_objects
tools.description: Permanently delete objects from the file by their IDs.

objectIds.description: Array of object IDs to delete.

tools.name: rename_objects
tools.description: Rename objects by their IDs.

renames.description: List of id/name pairs to rename.

name.description: The new name for the object.

tools.name: select_objects
tools.description: Select objects in the editor by their IDs. Pass an empty array to clear the selection.

objectIds.description: Array of object IDs to select in the editor. Pass an empty array to clear the selection.

tools.name: duplicate_objects
tools.description: Duplicate objects by their IDs. Copies are placed as siblings of the originals.

objectIds.description: Array of object IDs to duplicate. Copies are placed as siblings of the originals.

tools.name: reorder_objects
tools.description: Change draw order (z-order): sendToFront, bringForward, sendBackward, or sendToBack.

operations.description: List of reorder operations to apply in order.

order.description: sendToFront: draw on top of all siblings; bringForward: move one step toward the front; sendBackward: move one step toward the back; sendToBack: draw behind all siblings.

tools.name: reparent_objects
tools.description: Move objects to a different parent in the hierarchy.

operations.description: List of reparent operations to apply.

newParentId.description: The ID of the new parent (must be a container: artboard, group, or layout).

position.description: Where to insert within the new parent. start = front (on top), end = back (behind). Defaults to end.

tools.name: manage_scripts
tools.description: Manages the LIFECYCLE of script and shader files: create, rename, move between folders, delete. Use this for any script/shader file-level operation. Does NOT edit script contents — to modify a script's source code, use text_editor. Commands: create: Creates one or more new Luau scripts or WGSL shaders, optionally seeded with content; rename: Renames one or more scripts/shaders by id or path (leaf name only — to relocate, use move); move: Moves one or more scripts/shaders to a target folder (missing folders are created); delete: Deletes one or more scripts/shaders.

name.description: Optional. Slashes group the script into folders, e.g. "utils/Math3D" places "Math3D" inside a "utils" folder (created if missing, reused on exact case-sensitive match). Trailing ".lua" / ".luau" / ".wgsl" / ".txt" is stripped automatically.

code_file_type.description: "luau" creates a Luau script (behavior, logic, converters, etc.). "wgsl" creates a shader for use with the GPU canvas. Defaults to "luau".

content.description: Optional initial source. When omitted, Luau scripts get the boilerplate for their protocol (or empty for utility) and shaders start empty. Prefer seeding here over creating empty and following up with text_editor.

scriptId.description: The id of the script/shader to rename.

scriptPath.description: Current path of the script/shader, e.g. "utils/Math3D". Use either scriptId or scriptPath.

newName.description: New leaf name only — no slashes. To relocate the file, use the move command instead.

scriptId.description: The id of the script/shader to move.

scriptPath.description: Current path of the script/shader, e.g. "utils/Math3D". Use either scriptId or scriptPath.

targetFolder.description: Destination folder path, e.g. "utils/math3d". Empty string or omitted moves to the workspace root. Folders are created if missing (mirrors create).

scriptId.description: The id of the script/shader to delete.

scriptPath.description: Path of the script/shader to delete, e.g. "utils/Math3D". Use either scriptId or scriptPath.

tools.name: text_editor
tools.description: View and edit EXISTING scripts in the workspace. STRICTLY for reading and modifying files that already exist. Do NOT use this tool to create new scripts — use create_script instead.

command.description:
The command to execute:
- view: View an existing file's contents
- str_replace: Replace text in an EXISTING file (file must already exist)
- insert: Append text to an EXISTING file (file must already exist)

path.description: The file path to operate on

old_string.description: The text to replace (for str_replace command)

view_range.description: Optional range of lines to view (1-indexed, inclusive). If provided, returns only the specified line range with line numbers prepended as "lineNumber: line".

tools.name: script_diagnostics
tools.description: Get analysis/linter errors and warnings from either a specific script if "path" is provided or all diagnostics for every script in the workspace if no path is provided

path.description: The file path to retrieve diagnostics (errors and warnings) for.

tools.name: get_scripts
tools.description: Lists all editable code files in the workspace — both Luau scripts and WGSL shaders. Each entry includes the module name, language ("luau" or "wgsl"), and (for Luau) the script protocol.

tools.name: run_tests
tools.description: Runs the tests for a given Tests script

path.description: The file path to the script to run tests for

tools.name: recompile_all_scripts
tools.description: Recompiles all scripts and updates their bytecode, committing all changes to the Luau virtual machine.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Searches for a pattern across editable code files in the workspace (Luau scripts AND WGSL shaders), similar to the grep command. Returns matching lines with their line numbers. If inclusion_set is provided, only the specified files are searched, otherwise all non-built-in files are searched. Supports case-sensitive matching, whole word matching, and regular expressions.

inclusion_set.description: Optional list of script or shader names to limit the search to. If not provided, all non-built-in files are searched.

case_sensitive.description: Whether the search should be case sensitive

match_whole_word.description: Whether to match whole words only

regular_expression.description: Whether the pattern should be treated as a regular expression

tools.name: read_console
tools.description:
Reads console output from script execution. Use this to examine print statements and errors from Rive scripts.

IMPORTANT: The console only contains output from script executions that have already occurred. If you need to see output from a specific operation:
1. Ask the user to perform the action that triggers the script (e.g., play the animation, interact with the state machine)
2. Once they confirm the action is complete, use this tool to read the results.

You can filter results by script name, entry type (print/error), or search for specific text within the output.

script_name.description: Filter entries to only those from this script

entry_type.description: Filter by entry type: 'print' for standard output, 'error' for errors

text_search.description: Case-insensitive search for text within console output

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 100)

offset.description: Number of matching entries to skip (for pagination)

reverse.description: When true, returns results in reverse order (newest first). Use with limit to get the most recent entries.

tools.name: get_scripting_reference
tools.description:
Retrieve Rive scripting API definitions and code examples. Use this to look up type definitions before writing code.

Request a topic key such as a builtin definition (e.g. "rive/paint", "rive/vector"), "viewmodel_definitions", "example_node", or "example_test". Use "viewmodel_definitions" when working with ViewModel data.
